result:
I have been thinking about how strange it is that we memorize the way to the grocery store but forget the name of the street we grew up on. Memory is not a library, it's a junk drawer. Some things are polished and easy to find, others are buried under receipts and broken chargers.

Morning light does that thing in my kitchen where it hits the chipped mug and makes it look intentional. I drink coffee too fast because I'm always pretending I have somewhere to be. The truth is most days I have nowhere urgent to go, just a list of small kindnesses I want to remember to do: text my sister, water the plant that is definitely dying, leave the porch light on.

I love the way cities smell after rain, metallic and clean. I love how strangers can be kind without it meaning anything. A barista remembers my order once and it feels like a small miracle. Then I realize I'm asking for permanence from people who are just trying to get through a shift.

Maybe freedom is not the big dramatic choice. It's the quiet permission to not be productive. To sit on the floor and read a book I already read. To let a song play twice without skipping.

I think about the people who will find my things later. Will they know I kept a paperclip collection? Probably not. And that's okay. We don't leave legacies, we leave crumbs. Small traces of warmth. That's enough.
